question.text: The integral $\int_0^\pi \frac{(x+3) \sin x}{1+3 \cos ^2 x} d x$ is equal to :

solution.text: $\begin{aligned} & I=\int_0^\pi \frac{(x+3) \sin x}{1+3 \cos ^2 x} d x \\ & I=\int_0^\pi \frac{(\pi-x+3) \sin x}{\left(1+3 \cos ^2 x\right)} d x \\ & 2 I=\int_0^\pi \frac{(\pi+6) \sin x \cdot d x}{\left(1+3 \cos ^2 x\right)}=2 \int_0^{\pi / 2} \frac{(\pi+6) \sin x}{\left(1+3 \cos ^2 x\right)} \\ & I=\int_0^{\pi / 2} \frac{(\pi+6) \sin x \cdot d x}{\left(1+3 \cos ^2 x\right)}=\frac{\pi}{3 \sqrt{3}}(\pi+6) \\ & \sqrt{3} \cos x=t \\ & \sqrt{3} \sin x=d t\end{aligned}$
